name: Tour du Mont Blanc
summary: A circuit of about 165 km around the Mont Blanc massif through France, Italy and Switzerland, usually walked anti-clockwise from Les Houches and staying in refuges and valley villages. The high point is the Col des Fours, with the Fenetre d'Arpette variant at the same height.

name: Walker's Haute Route
summary: The walking route from Chamonix to Zermatt, roughly 220 km over eleven or more cols, with the Col de Prafleuri as its highest point. It stays below 3,000 m and needs no rope or crampons, but the terrain is rocky, remote and sustained.

name: Chamonix–Zermatt Haute Route
summary: The original Haute Route, a glacier crossing from Chamonix to Zermatt done on ski touring gear in spring, with Tete Blanche as its high point. Large sections are on glacier and it requires roped travel and mountaineering experience, not walking fitness alone.

name: Tour du Matterhorn
summary: A circuit of about 150 km around the Matterhorn between the Valais and the Aosta Valley, crossing the Theodul Pass on its glacier. Several cols are near or above 3,000 m and two crossings are glaciated, so it is a step beyond an ordinary hut-to-hut walk.

name: Tour des Combins
summary: A loop of roughly 100 km around the Grand Combin, from Bourg-Saint-Pierre through the Val de Bagnes and the Italian Valpelline and back over the Fenetre de Durand. The Col des Otanes above the Corbassiere glacier is the high point; longer 'Grand Tour' variants run to about 140 km.

name: Tour de la Vanoise
summary: A hut-to-hut loop through the Vanoise National Park in the Savoie, using sections of the GR5 and GR55 between Pralognan, Modane and Tignes. It finishes over the Col de Chaviere, the highest col crossed by any GR route in France.

name: Tour du Queyras
summary: The GR58, a circuit of about 130 km around the Queyras regional park in the southern French Alps, linking villages and refuges over a series of cols. The Col de Chamoussiere is the highest point; nothing on the route is technical.

name: Via Alpina
country: Italy / Slovenia / Austria / Germany / Liechtenstein / Switzerland / France / Monaco
summary: A waymarked network across the whole Alpine chain from Trieste to Monaco, built as an Alpine Convention project and divided into well over a hundred day stages. Its highest point is the Niederjoch above Vent; almost nobody walks the whole thing in one season, and stages range from valley paths to high glacier cols.

name: Stubai High Trail
summary: The Stubaier Hoehenweg, a circular hut route of about 80 km linking eight huts around the head of the Stubai valley in Tyrol. It is graded a black trail: sections are secured with cable and steel steps, and it needs sure footing and a head for heights.

name: Berlin High Trail
summary: The Berliner Hoehenweg, a hut circuit of roughly 70 km above Mayrhofen in the Zillertal Alps, from the Gamshuette round to the Edelhuette. The Schoenbichler Horn is the high point, and the route includes cabled sections, boulder fields and snow patches that persist into summer.

name: Zillertal Alps High Trail
summary: Zillertaler Hoehenweg and Zillertaler Runde are alternative names for the Berliner Hoehenweg, the same hut circuit through the Zillertal Alps high nature park with the Schoenbichler Horn as its high point. It is listed separately only because the German and English names are both in common use.

name: Adlerweg
summary: Tyrol's Eagle Walk, about 420 km in 33 stages: 24 across North Tyrol from St Johann to the Arlberg, plus a separate nine-stage arm in East Tyrol. Most walkers take a section rather than the whole trail; one pass, the Eppzirler Scharte, is markedly harder than the rest and can be avoided.

name: E5 Alpine Crossing
summary: The popular section of the E5 long-distance path, about 80 km from Oberstdorf in the Allgaeu over the main Alpine watershed to Meran in South Tyrol. The Pitztaler Joechl is the high point and often holds snow; a bus or lift is used on some stages in most commercial itineraries.

name: Gran Paradiso Trek
summary: The Alta Via 2 of the Aosta Valley, running from Courmayeur to Donnas in fourteen stages through the Gran Paradiso National Park and the Mont Avic park. Its highest point is the Col Lauson above Valnontey; the route does not climb Gran Paradiso itself.

name: Tour of the Bernina
summary: A circuit of roughly 100 to 120 km around the Bernina massif, crossing between the Engadine in Graubuenden and Valmalenco and Valposchiavo in Lombardy. Itineraries differ and the name is also used for Swiss national route 53, a shorter five-stage line from Poschiavo to Maloja.
